description: Labeled vulnerability corpus for the hack:benchmark accuracy gate. Each sample contains exactly one intentional vulnerability (or none, for clean samples). Lines refer to the 1-indexed location of the vulnerable statement. accepted_types lists TRUE synonyms of the canonical type — only types that name the SAME underlying flaw (e.g. dynamic_column_injection is a flavour of sql_injection; idor and auth_bypass are both broken access control). Broad stand-ins such as missing_validation are NOT accepted, since crediting them would inflate per-type recall. A credited true positive is always reported under the ground-truth (canonical) type, never the synonym the AI happened to emit.
measurement_caveat: THIS CORPUS IS SYNTHETIC AND WAS AUTHORED ALONGSIDE THE DETECTORS. Every sample is a textbook instance of its flaw, planted on purpose, and the routes that expose them are declared in routes.php by the same hand. The numbers this corpus produces are a RECALL CHECK — 'does the engine still find the bugs it is supposed to find' — and a regression gate for detection changes. They are NOT a precision claim about real code: nothing here has the ambiguity, the framework idioms or the deliberate-by-design patterns that generate false positives in a real application. Precision is measured separately, on unmodified third-party Laravel applications.
engines: Each expectation names the engine the gate holds responsible for it. 'deterministic' = the reproducible, provider-independent detectors are expected to find it with no AI in the loop (this is what `hack:benchmark --deterministic` scores). 'ai' = only the AI pass is expected to find it. The tag is a floor, not a ceiling: a deterministic detector that also finds an 'ai'-tagged label is credited in full-corpus mode.
routes: Every controller sample is routed by tests/Fixtures/benchmark/routes.php. The access-control engine will not report a record exposure it cannot attribute to a routed entry point, so a sample with no route entry is UNMEASURED, not clean. BenchmarkCorpusTest fails when one goes missing.
